cards.front: Define the "period" ($T$) of an oscillation or wave. What are its standard SI units?
cards.back: The period ($T$) is the time taken for one complete cycle of an oscillation or wave to occur. Its standard SI unit is seconds (s).

cards.front: Define the "frequency" ($f$) of an oscillation or wave. What are its standard SI units?
cards.back: The frequency ($f$) is the number of complete cycles of an oscillation or wave that occur per unit time. Its standard SI unit is Hertz (Hz), which is equivalent to $s^{-1}$ (cycles per second).

cards.front: State the fundamental mathematical relationship between the period ($T$) and frequency ($f$) of an oscillation or wave.
cards.back:
The period ($T$) and frequency ($f$) are reciprocals of each other:
$$f = \frac{1}{T}$$
$$T = \frac{1}{f}$$

cards.front: Define "angular frequency" ($\omega$) in the context of oscillations. How does it relate to circular motion? What are its standard SI units?
cards.back: Angular frequency ($\omega$) represents the rate of change of the phase of a sinusoidal waveform, or the angular displacement per unit time for an object in uniform circular motion. One complete cycle corresponds to an angular displacement of $2\pi$ radians. Its standard SI unit is radians per second (rad/s), which is dimensionally equivalent to $s^{-1}$.

cards.front: Derive or state the relationship between angular frequency ($\omega$) and frequency ($f$). Explain the $2\pi$ factor.
cards.back:
Since one complete cycle corresponds to an angular displacement of $2\pi$ radians, and frequency ($f$) is the number of cycles per second, the angular frequency ($\omega$) is given by:
$$\omega = 2\pi f$$
The $2\pi$ factor converts cycles per second ($f$) into radians per second ($\omega$), as there are $2\pi$ radians in one full cycle.

cards.front: Derive or state the relationship between angular frequency ($\omega$) and period ($T$).
cards.back:
We know that $\omega = 2\pi f$ and $f = 1/T$. Substituting the expression for $f$ into the equation for $\omega$:
$$\omega = 2\pi \left(\frac{1}{T}\right)$$
$$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$$

cards.front: A pendulum completes 10 full oscillations in 20 seconds. Calculate its frequency ($f$), period ($T$), and angular frequency ($\omega$).
cards.back:
1.  **Frequency ($f$)**:
    $f = \frac{\text{Number of oscillations}}{\text{Time taken}} = \frac{10 \text{ cycles}}{20 \text{ s}} = 0.5 \text{ Hz}$
2.  **Period ($T$)**:
    $T = \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{0.5 \text{ Hz}} = 2 \text{ s}$
    (Alternatively: $T = \frac{\text{Time taken}}{\text{Number of oscillations}} = \frac{20 \text{ s}}{10 \text{ cycles}} = 2 \text{ s}$)
3.  **Angular Frequency ($\omega$)**:
    $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi (0.5 \text{ Hz}) = \pi \text{ rad/s} \approx 3.14 \text{ rad/s}$
    (Alternatively: $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T} = \frac{2\pi}{2 \text{ s}} = \pi \text{ rad/s}$)
